1	# Contract: `CreateEntryUseCase` / `EntriesRepository.create` / `EntriesRemoteDataSource.create` extension
2	
3	Extends the interface `specs/003-multimodal-capture/contracts/entries-repository.md` and
4	`specs/003-multimodal-capture/contracts/save-usecases.md` already define — `create`'s existing two required
5	parameters (`content`, `source`) are unchanged; this unit only adds two optional named ones, exactly the
6	extension `create_entry_usecase.dart`'s own doc comment has named since RF01 shipped.
7	
8	```dart
9	class CreateEntryUseCase {
10	  const CreateEntryUseCase(this._repository);
11	  final EntriesRepository _repository;
12	
13	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> call(
14	    String content,
15	    EntrySource source, {
16	    String? chatMessageId,
17	    DateTime? occurredAt,
18	  }) => _repository.create(
19	    content: content,
20	    source: source,
21	    chatMessageId: chatMessageId,
22	    occurredAt: occurredAt,
23	  );
24	}
25	```
26	
27	```dart
28	abstract class EntriesRepository {
29	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({
30	    required String content,
31	    required EntrySource source,
32	    String? chatMessageId,
33	    DateTime? occurredAt,
34	  });
35	  // list / getById / search / cachedEntries — unchanged, see 003/005/006's own contracts
36	}
37	```
38	
39	## `EntriesRepositoryImpl.create()` (orchestration, data layer) — unchanged shape, 2 new pass-through params
40	
41	```dart
42	Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({
43	  required String content,
44	  required EntrySource source,
45	  String? chatMessageId,
46	  DateTime? occurredAt,
47	}) async {
48	  await _ensureLocalCacheLoaded();
49	  final result = await _remoteDataSource.create(
50	    content: content,
51	    source: source,
52	    chatMessageId: chatMessageId,
53	    occurredAt: occurredAt,
54	  );
55	  return result.match(
56	    (failure) => Future.value(Left(failure)),
57	    (entry) async {
58	      await _cacheAndPersist([entry]);
59	      return Right(entry);
60	    },
61	  );
62	}
63	```
64	
65	No retry-on-`AuthExpiredFailure` is added here (research.md R9) — `create()` has never had one (RF01), and
66	this unit doesn't add it; `ChatBloc`'s own `_onBookmarkTapped` fires `reauthRequired` on that specific failure
67	instead (contracts/chat-bloc-bookmark-extension.md).
68	
69	## `EntriesRemoteDataSource.create()` (data layer) — request body gains 2 optional fields
70	
71	```dart
72	Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({
73	  required String content,
74	  required EntrySource source,
75	  String? chatMessageId,
76	  DateTime? occurredAt,
77	}) async {
78	  final result = await _apiClient.call(
79	    'entries-create',
80	    method: 'POST',
81	    body: {
82	      'content': content,
83	      'source': source.name,
84	      if (chatMessageId != null) 'chatMessageId': chatMessageId,
85	      if (occurredAt != null) 'occurredAt': occurredAt.toUtc().toIso8601String(),
86	    },
87	  );
88	  return result.flatMap(_parseEntry);   // unchanged — Entry.chatMessageId/occurredAt already parsed since RF01
89	}
90	```
91	
92	The class's own doc comment ("Never sends `occurredAt`/`mediaDurationSeconds`/`chatMessageId` in a request
93	body") is updated to drop `occurredAt`/`chatMessageId` from that list — `mediaDurationSeconds` still never
94	sent by any caller in this app.
95	
96	## Who depends on this
97	
98	`ChatBloc._onBookmarkTapped` (contracts/chat-bloc-bookmark-extension.md) is the only new caller, passing both
99	new parameters. Every existing caller — `SaveTextEntryUseCase`, `ConfirmEntrySaveUseCase` (RF01/RF02) — omits
100	both and is unaffected.
101	
102	## Test scenarios this contract owns (RNF07/RNF09 — for `/speckit-tasks` to schedule, not built here)
103	
104	| # | Scenario | Expected |
105	|---|---|---|
106	| 1 | `create(content, EntrySource.manual)` — no new params | Request body unchanged (no `chatMessageId`/`occurredAt` keys) — confirms zero regression for every existing caller |
107	| 2 | `create(content, EntrySource.chat, chatMessageId: 'uuid-1', occurredAt: t)` | Request body includes both: `{'chatMessageId': 'uuid-1', 'occurredAt': t.toUtc().toIso8601String()}` alongside `content`/`source` |
108	| 3 | `create(..., chatMessageId: 'uuid-1')` without `occurredAt` | Only `chatMessageId` added; no `occurredAt` key present |
109	| 4 | Backend responds `200` with an entry whose `chatMessageId` equals a value already saved once before (simulating the idempotent-retry path) | `Right(Entry(...))` parsed normally — no special client-side handling needed; `_cacheAndPersist` upserts by `id`, same as any other `create()` result |
110	| 5 | `create()` fails `NetworkOfflineFailure`/`NetworkTimeoutFailure`/`ValidationFailure` (the 3 RNF09 scenarios, already covered by RF01's own tests for this endpoint) | `Left(<that failure>)`, unchanged — confirms the extension didn't alter existing failure-mapping behavior |
111	| 6 | `create()` fails `AuthExpiredFailure` | `Left(AuthExpiredFailure)` — no silent retry attempted inside `EntriesRepositoryImpl.create()` itself (research.md R9); the caller (`ChatBloc`) is responsible for any reauth signaling |

# Quickstart: P-RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry

How to validate this unit end-to-end once implemented, mapped to spec.md's four user stories. A run guide —
interfaces are in `contracts/`, state/entities in `data-model.md`.

## Prerequisites

- RF01 and RF04 already implemented and passing — a signed-in test account can reach `/home`, send chat
  messages, and (separately) create entries via the Insertion Modal.
- At least one existing conversation with 2+ user messages, for Story 2's "save twice" and Story 4's
  "assistant has no bookmark" checks.
- A way to force a write failure for Story 3 (airplane mode toggled right before a tap, or a test double at
  the repository layer for automated tests) and, separately, a way to force an `AUTH_EXPIRED` response for the
  reauth-overlay Edge Case.
- A way to clear/forget this device's local chat cache (reinstall, or a debug-only cache-clear action) to
  exercise FR-004's "no local record of a prior success" path without needing a second physical device.

## Automated checks

```bash
fvm flutter analyze                                    # RNF06 import-shape lint
fvm flutter test --coverage
lcov --extract coverage/lcov.info 'lib/**/domain/**' -o coverage/domain.info
genhtml coverage/domain.info -o coverage/domain-html    # RNF07 gate — bookmark_status.dart, _seedBookmarks, etc.
dart test/architecture/no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart   # ChatBloc stays within lib/features/chat/
dart test/architecture/domain_purity_test.dart          # chat/domain/ imports neither Flutter nor chat/data/
```

`contracts/create-entry-usecase-chat-extension.md`, `contracts/chat-repository-bookmark-extension.md`, and
`contracts/chat-bloc-bookmark-extension.md` each carry the full scenario table this unit's coverage depends
on.

## Manual verification (device/Simulator)

### Story 1 — Turning a message you just wrote into a journal entry (P1)

1. Send a message in an active conversation. **Expect**: a bookmark control (outline icon) appears next to
   that message only, in its `idle` state.
2. Tap it. **Expect**: it shows a spinner (`saving`), then settles into an ochre check (`saved`), with no
   visible delay beyond the network round-trip.
3. Open "Meus Registros" (or wherever entries are listed). **Expect**: a new entry exists with that message's
   exact text as content, `source` = `chat`, and `chatMessageId` matching the message — structurally
   indistinguishable from any RF01-captured entry otherwise.
4. Leave the conversation (side menu → another screen) and come back, then fully restart the app and reopen
   it. **Expect**: the same message's bookmark still shows the ochre check, not reset to `idle` (FR-008).

### Story 2 — Saving the same message twice never creates a duplicate (P1)

1. On an already-`saved` bookmark, confirm it has no tap affordance at all (no visual "pressed" feedback, no
   network call fires even if tapped where the icon renders). **Expect**: exactly one entry still exists for
   that message afterward.
2. Clear/forget the device's local chat cache (or reinstall), then reopen the same conversation. **Expect**:
   the previously-saved message's bookmark renders `idle` again (the local record is gone) — tap it.
   **Expect**: it goes `saving` → `saved` again, and "Meus Registros" still shows exactly one entry for that
   message, never two (the backend's own idempotency, confirmed via `error-taxonomy.md`'s "never `409`, always
   `200`").

### Story 3 — A failed save never disrupts the conversation (P2)

1. Enable airplane mode, then tap an `idle` bookmark. **Expect**: `saving` briefly, then a red warning icon
   (`error`) — never stuck in `saving`.
2. While that bookmark is still `error`, send a new message, scroll the conversation, and tap a *different*
   message's bookmark (also while still offline, to confirm it independently reaches `error` too).
   **Expect**: every one of those actions works normally — sending still optimistically appends (and then
   itself fails/blocks per RF04's own offline behavior, unrelated to the bookmark), scrolling is unaffected,
   the second bookmark reaches its own `error` independently.
3. Disable airplane mode, then tap the first failed bookmark again. **Expect**: it re-attempts (`saving`) and
   reaches `saved`.
4. Force a session expiration (`AUTH_EXPIRED`) while a bookmark save is in flight. **Expect**: the existing
   "Sessão expirada" overlay appears over the chat (Edge Cases); the bookmark itself ends in `error`
   (retryable) rather than stuck in `saving`; after re-authenticating, tapping it again succeeds normally.

### Story 4 — Only your own messages can become entries (P2)

1. In a conversation with both user and assistant messages (including at least one streaming/in-progress and
   one failed assistant response, if reachable), inspect every message. **Expect**: a bookmark control is
   present on every user message and absent from every single assistant one, with no exceptions.

### Edge cases worth exercising manually at least once

- Tap a bookmark twice in rapid succession before the first tap's request resolves. **Expect**: only one
  network call fires (observable via a debug network log or a single spinner-to-settled transition, not a
  flicker of two).
- Tap the bookmark on a message the instant after sending it (before the composer's optimistic placeholder has
  been reconciled with the backend's real message id — a very narrow window, may require a slow/throttled
  connection to reliably hit). **Expect**: the tap is silently ignored; tapping again a moment later (once the
  message has a real id) works normally (research.md R6).
- A message's content at or near the entry content-length limit. **Expect**: the save either succeeds
  normally, or — if the backend's own validation rejects it — the bookmark shows `error` without crashing or
  silently dropping the attempt.
- Navigate away from a conversation while a bookmark save is in flight, then return to it. **Expect**: the
  bookmark reflects the save's actual outcome (`saved` or `error`), never a stale `saving` indicator tied to a
  request that already finished.

I've loaded and cross-checked spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md, data-model.md, the three contracts, quickstart.md, and the constitution, plus verified two claims against the actual architecture-test code in the repo. Here's the analysis.

## Specification Analysis Report

| ID | Category | Severity | Location(s) | Summary | Recommendation |
|----|----------|----------|-------------|---------|----------------|
| C1 | Coverage Gap / Inconsistency | HIGH | tasks.md:12-15 (Tests intro), tasks.md:401-405 (T044), contracts/chat-bloc-bookmark-extension.md:158-171 (scenarios 7-10) | `chat-bloc-bookmark-extension.md`'s scenario table has 10 numbered test scenarios. Tasks only schedule automated coverage for scenarios 1,2,3,4,5,6 (via T024/T028/T032/T033/T034). Scenarios **7** (tap on optimistic message), **8** (defensive tap on assistant message), **9** (navigate-away mid-save), and **10** (reload shows `saved` after a real round trip, i.e. FR-008/SC-005's actual mechanism) have no corresponding task anywhere in Phases 2-7. Scenario 7 and 10 only appear as *manual* quickstart steps (quickstart.md:84-93); scenario 8 and 9 appear nowhere, not even manually. Yet T044 explicitly claims "every scenario... has a corresponding passing test from T008/T012/T013/T024/T028/T030/T032-T034/T036" — that task list maps to only 6 of the 10 chat-bloc scenarios, so T044 will fail its own cross-check as written, and the tasks.md intro's promise ("Every contract's own scenario table is scheduled below") is false for this contract. | Add 2 tasks (e.g. T034a/T034b) to Phase 3/5 for scenarios 7-9 in `chat_bloc_test.dart`, and one task to Phase 3 (alongside T024) for scenario 10 (the actual save→`recordMessageSaved`→`ConversationSelected` reload round trip) — this is the only scenario that automatically verifies FR-008/SC-005's real mechanism rather than a hand-seeded map. Then correct T044's covering-task list. |
| I1 | Inconsistency | MEDIUM | plan.md:123,215-217; tasks.md:172-177 (T016), 390-393 (T042); test/architecture/no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart; test/architecture/domain_purity_test.dart | FR-009 requires `ChatBloc` (a `presentation/bloc/` file) to never import `EntriesRepository`/`EntriesRemoteDataSource` directly. Plan.md and T016/T042 both assert this is "confirmed against `no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart`"/`domain_purity_test.dart`.
